card.name: Vitamin intake and nutrient amounts
card.fires_on: Punctuation, digits and small linking words inside general nutrition text about vitamins such as niacin, folate and vitamin E. It fires at points where a daily amount or a source of the nutrient is about to be given.

modes.label: Amounts in vitamin text
modes.description: Digits or unit pieces inside daily-intake figures for a vitamin.
modes.example: The DRI for niacin is 14–<<1>>6 mg per day in adults.

modes.label: Linking words after vitamin names
modes.description: A comma, bracket or verb right after a vitamin or nutrient name, before a description of its forms or role.
modes.example: Niacin comes in two forms<<,>> nicotinic acid and nicotin

card.writes: It seems to push toward words meaning 'from' or 'source' (as in sources of a nutrient) and away from words about humans or life.
card.plain: It lights up in nutrition passages on vitamins, where the text is about to say how much or where the nutrient comes from.
